title: Do Architects in Westchester Handle Permits? Here's What You Need to Know
excerpt: Yes, architects in Westchester handle permits, but it depends on who you hire. Learn what a design-build firm can do for your project from start to finish.
content:
If you're planning a home renovation in Westchester County, you've probably wondered who handles all those permits and inspections. The short answer is yes, architects can handle permits. But the real question is whether yours will actually take that responsibility off your plate or leave you to figure it out yourself.

Permit work isn't glamorous, and some architects won't touch it. That's where hiring the right team makes all the difference. When you work with a licensed architect in Westchester who is also a general contractor, you get someone who knows both sides of the process and can guide you through it.

Why Permits Matter in Westchester

Every town in Westchester County has its own building department and its own permit process. Scarsdale has one set of requirements. White Plains has another. Rye, Pelham, Mamaroneck, and Larchmont all operate their own systems. This isn't unique or difficult. It's just how things work here.

What matters is that permits exist for a reason. They protect your home, ensure the work is done safely, and keep your property value intact. Skipping permits or doing the work wrong can create serious problems down the road. You could face code violations, fail an inspection, or have trouble selling your home later.

What a Design-Build Firm Actually Does

A design-build approach in Westchester means one firm handles both the design and construction. That person or team knows exactly what they're planning to build and how to build it. They can coordinate with your local building department before construction even starts.

At House Architecture & Construction, Silvio M. Luca runs every project personally. He's a licensed New York architect and a licensed general contractor. That means he pulls the permits, submits the plans, manages inspections, and handles any issues that come up. He knows what each town wants to see because he works in Eastchester, Hastings-on-Hudson, Tarrytown, Ossining, Dobbs Ferry, and across Westchester County.

When you hire someone who understands both architecture and construction, permits stop being a headache. They become part of the natural workflow.

Your Role in the Permit Process

You're not off the hook entirely. You'll need to approve the designs, understand what's being proposed, and make decisions about your project. But the paperwork, the submittals, the back-and-forth with the building department? That's handled for you.

Whether you're planning home additions in Westchester, a primary suite addition, a kitchen remodel, or a complete historic restoration, the permit process works the same way. Your architect needs to prepare plans, submit them for approval, get them stamped, and coordinate inspections as work progresses.

Having a residential architect in Scarsdale or anywhere else in Westchester who actually takes responsibility for permits means fewer delays and fewer surprises. You get professional guidance and peace of mind.
